name: Student Feedback Emotion Analysis
description: Local emotion classification with contextual analytics, labeled evaluation, human review, and monitoring.
summary: A pinned English model classifies feedback locally. Labeled evaluation, annotation queues, and reference/current monitoring help inspect model outputs without treating them as evidence of a student’s mental state.
architecture: Streamlit manages dataset intake, evaluation, annotation, and monitoring snapshots. A pinned Hugging Face DistilRoBERTa model executes locally on CPU through Transformers/PyTorch. Pandas prepares and aggregates results; Plotly visualizes contextual trends. Human review does not retrain the model.

capabilities.name: Emotion classification
capabilities.description: Batch-classify usable English feedback into seven labels with low-confidence flags.

capabilities.name: Labeled evaluation
capabilities.description: Inspect supplied-label accuracy, F1, confusion matrices, errors, and ambiguity.

capabilities.name: Human review and monitoring
capabilities.description: Annotate results, export curated records, and compare reference/current snapshots.

stack.usage: Separate pages coordinate analysis, evaluation, annotations, and monitoring state.
Python modules validate uploads and orchestrate independent analysis and monitoring snapshots.
Transformers loads j-hartmann/emotion-english-distilroberta-base at a fixed revision for batched classification.
PyTorch runs the pretrained model locally rather than sending feedback to hosted inference.
DataFrames preserve original rows and support context summaries, annotations, and exports.
Interactive figures show emotion distributions, contextual patterns, and monitoring comparisons.
Metrics compare predicted emotion labels with supplied reference labels.

architectureConnections.description: The pinned classifier runs through the local CPU runtime.
Prepared emotion results and snapshot summaries feed charts.
